- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or shows recent volatility, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged overshoot; cap forecast at +10% above peak for next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70.5–71.0), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of recent history.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates the 1st–3rd day; reduce first 3 forecast points by 0.5–1.5% relative to true outcome.
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.7), model often fails to adjust; force a 1–2% downward correction in next 3–5 days.
